context: Rejection coverage for a handler where the interesting content is the status vocabulary and the order of the checks. Predicted baseline failure: the agent produces a competent-looking file in which a wrong media type, an oversized body and unparseable JSON all expect 400, because 'the client sent something bad' maps to 400 by reflex - and, since the fixture returns 415, 411 and 413 for those, several of its cases simply fail, or it reads them off the source one at a time without ever testing which check wins when two apply. The ordering facts are the part a rejection sweep never reaches: an oversized body is refused before the parser sees it, a bad signature is refused before the parser sees it, a wrong media type outranks the size check, and the size is counted in UTF-8 bytes rather than characters.

checklist.name: Test file created
checklist.description: A file src/receiveWebhook.test.js exists and contains at least one rejection case. A file that only repeats the accepted ping scores zero.

checklist.name: Each rejection keeps its own status
checklist.description: The suite asserts 415 for a missing or unsupported media type and an unsupported charset, 411 for a missing length header, 400 for a length mismatch and for unparseable JSON, 413 for an oversized body, 401 for a bad signature, and 422 for a parsed body of the wrong shape. Any case that expects a generic 400 where the handler returns 411, 413, 415 or 422 scores zero, as does a suite that asserts one shared status for the envelope family.

checklist.name: The body is proven unread when it is refused early
checklist.description: One case sends an oversized body that is also invalid JSON and asserts 413 with PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, and another sends invalid JSON with a wrong signature and asserts 401 with SIGNATURE_INVALID. Each shows the parser was never reached. Neither case present scores zero; one of the two scores at most half.

checklist.name: Size is counted in bytes
checklist.description: A case sends a body whose character count is below MAX_BYTES but whose UTF-8 byte length is above it - accented or other multi-byte characters, with Content-Length set to the byte length - and asserts 413. Sizing every case with String.length only scores zero: it is the partner incident described in the task.

checklist.name: Check order asserted where two refusals apply
checklist.description: A case sends an oversized body with a non-JSON media type and asserts 415 rather than 413, showing the media-type check runs first. Omitting any such case scores zero.

checklist.name: Charset handled as its own rejection
checklist.description: A case sends application/json with a charset other than utf-8 and asserts 415 with CHARSET_UNSUPPORTED, distinct from the missing and unsupported media-type cases. Folding it into the media-type case scores zero.

checklist.name: Post-parse shape rejections covered
checklist.description: Cases send a valid JSON array or scalar asserting 422 with BODY_NOT_AN_OBJECT and a valid object with a non-string event asserting 422 with EVENT_REQUIRED. Covering neither scores zero; expecting 400 for these scores at most half.

checklist.name: MUST NOT assert rejection by exclusion or by message text
checklist.description: No case asserts merely that the status is not 202, that it is at least 400, or that a code or message string is present or contains some phrase. Every case names the exact status and the exact code constant. Any case relying on a not-equal, truthiness or substring check scores zero on this criterion.
